data.exact_reserve_text: During 2016 the Syndicate released GBP 95.7m of technical reserves in respect of prior periods (2015: GBP 95.7m), arising predominantly from the Energy and Treaty Divisions. These releases were due to favourable claims development on losses during 2016.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Estimated ultimate gross claims GBP 11.8m (net GBP 9.7m); after allowing for inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to GBP 8.6m.
Flooding that hit the UK in November and December 2015 (mentioned as one of the largest 2015 events).

named_events.loss_description: Current estimated ultimate claims for this event are GBP 10.9m and GBP 7.7m gross and net of reinsurance. After allowing for inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to GBP 7.3m.
Exposure to an earthquake in the North Canterbury district of New Zealand in November (GBP 5.7m net of inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums).
Exposure to an earthquake in the Esmeraldas province of Ecuador in April (GBP 5.4m net of inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums).
Described as the costliest natural catastrophe of the year (earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan, April 2016).
Hurricane Matthew bringing widespread destruction and loss of life across a number of Caribbean Islands; insured losses estimated to be in excess of $5bn for the season context.

named_events.event_name: Tullow Oil Kwame Nkrumah vessel loss
named_events.loss_description: Tullow Oil Kwame Nkrumah vessel off the coast of Ghana affected performance (mentioned in Energy commentary).
Explosions at a warehouse in the port of Tianjin in China in August 2015; estimated ultimate claims gross GBP 11.8m and net GBP 9.7m.

data.standardized_narrative: At the start of 2016 gross claims outstanding were GBP 1,609.0m. During 2016 the Syndicate recorded a significant prior-year release of GBP 95.7m driven predominantly by favourable claims development, principally in the Energy and Treaty divisions. The release reduced prior year reserves (release  -5.95% of opening gross claims). The syndicate nevertheless retained exposures to several 2016 catastrophe events (notably the Fort McMurray wildfires, North Canterbury and Ecuador earthquakes) which produced quantified net impacts in the single-digit millions on the syndicate's balances. Older events from 2015 (Tianjin and UK floods) are referenced as prior-year contributors to claims movements.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2016 the Syndicate released GBP 95.7m of technical reserves in respect of prior periods (2015: GBP 95.7m), arising predominantly from the Energy and Treaty Divisions.
These releases were due to favourable claims development on losses during 2016.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development amount taken from narrative 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' which states a release of GBP 95.7m; the note is explicit but does not show a GROSS-labelled column so there is some ambiguity whether the number quoted is gross or net-per report wording it is presented as a syndicate-level technical reserves release and has been used as the gross PYD here. Some event amounts cited in the reserves note are given as gross and net; where the report provided a final 'after reinstatement' figure that was used as the syndicate net impact. The claims development triangle was transcribed visually and approximated from the printed table; aggregate column '2010 & prior' excluded per instructions.
